newsitem.title: USA: Emerging mkt hedge funds outpace others - Feb report.
newsitem.headline: Emerging mkt hedge funds outpace others - Feb report.

text.p: U.S. hedge funds that specialize in emerging markets returned 11.7 percent on average in the first two months of this year, far surpassing the performance of all other hedge fund types and the S&P 500 through February, Van Hedge Fund Advisors reported on Monday.

"This exceptional performance is due largely to selective investments in the burgeoning stock markets of Russia, Hungary, Brazil, Poland and other emerging markets, excepting those in Asia which have tendered sub-par performance so far in 1997," said George Van, chairman of Van Hedge Fund Advisors.

Meanwhile, Van said the year-to-date average U.S. hedge fund gained 3.1 percent, while the average offshore hedge fund rose 5.5 percent. The report said the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average for the same period rose 7.1 percent and 7.0 percent, respectively.

In the month of February, the best performing hedge fund investment style was offshore short selling, which profited from volatility in small-cap stocks damaged by disappointing earnings reports, Van said. Fund managers employing that strategy had returns of 5.6 percent for the month, while U.S. short selling gained 5.4 percent in February, he said.

Other investment styles that rose strongly in February were U.S. emerging markets, up 5.0 percent on the month, offshore emerging markets, up 4.0 percent, market neutral arbitrage, up 3.2 percent and offshore fund of funds, up 2.8 percent.
Hedge funds are private investment partnerships with wide latitude to invest across a variety of financial markets, frequently using borrowed money and derivatives.
Van Hedge Fund Advisors bases its performance index on a database of about 2,400 hedge funds managing more than $100 billion in assets.
